<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|348|THE ACTES|CHA. XIX.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=19|verse=6}}† And vvhen Paul had {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Paul ministred the Sacrament of Confirmation. ''See annot. c. 8, 17''.}}∷ imposed hands on them, the holy Ghost came vpon them, and they spake vvith tongues, and prophecied. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=7}}† And all the men vvere about tvvelue.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=8}}† And entring in to the synagogue, he spake confidently for three moneths, disputing and exhorting of the kingdom of God.⊣ {{verse|chapter=19|verse=9}}† But vvhen certaine vvere indûrate, and beleeued not, il-speaking the vvay of our Lord before the multitude, departing from them, he separated the disciples, daily disputing in the schole of one Tyrannus. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=10}}† An this vvas done for the space of tvvo yeres, so that al vvhich dvvelt in Asia, heard the vvord of our Lord, Iewes and Gentils.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=11}}† And God vvrought by the hand of Paul miracles not common: {{verse|chapter=19|verse=12}}† so that there were also brought from his body {{sup|‖}} napkins or handkerchefs vpon the sicke, and the diseases departed from them, and the vvicked spirits vvent out. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=13}}† And certaine also of the Iudaical exorcists that vvent about, assaied to inuocate vpon them that had euil spirits, the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}}, saying, I adiure you by {{sc|Iesvs}} vvhom Paul preacheth. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=14}}† And there vvere certaine sonnes of Sceua a Iewe, cheefe priest, seuen, that did this. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=15}}† But the vvicked spirit answering, said to them, {{sc|Iesvs}} I know, and {{sup|‖}} Paul I knovv: but you, what are ye? {{verse|chapter=19|verse=16}}† And the man in whom the wicked spirit vvas, leaping vpon them, and mastring {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`them''}}`both', preuailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and vvounded. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=17}}† And this vvas made notorious to al the Iewes and the Gentiles that dwelt at Ephesus: and feare fel vpon al them, and the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas magnified. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=18}}† And many of them that beleeued, came confessing and declaring {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ They made not only a general confessiō wherein al mē shew thē selues alike to be sinners, as our Protestants do: but euery one confessed his owne proper deedes and faultes.}}∷ their deedes. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=19}}† And many of them that had folovved {{sup|‖}} curious things, brought together their {{sup|‖}} bookes, and burnt them before al: and counting the prices of them, they found the money to be fiftie thousand pence. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=20}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The 6. part.}}So mightely increased the vvord of God and vvas confirmed.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=21}}† And vvhen these things vvere ended, Paul purposed in the Spirit, vvhen he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to goe to Hierusalem, saying, After I shall haue been there, I must see {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The 6 part. Of taking away the Gospel from Hierusalem the head citie of the Iewes, and giuing it to Rome the head citie of the Gentils.}}Rome also. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=22}}† And sending into Macedonia tvvo of them that ministred vnto him, Timothee and Erastus, him self remained for a time in Asia.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=23}}† And at that time there vvas made no litle trouble<noinclude>{{rh|||about}}</noinclude>
